$comment: SCHEMA CONTRACT — the `labre_mcp` Postgres schema, as labre-mcp expects to find it.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The migrations that CREATE this schema live in the labre
repository (supabase/migrations/), because the Supabase project — and therefore
the single migration chain the CLI accepts — belongs to labre. But the schema is
read by THIS repository: src/lib/bundles/supabase-bundle-source.mts reads
labre_mcp.strategy_bundles, src/core/transport/api-key-auth.mts calls
labre_mcp.validate_api_key. Nothing mechanical connected the two before ARCH-26:
a column rename or a dropped grant landed in labre, shipped green there, and broke
labre-mcp in production. This file is the missing coupling. See ARCH-26 in
docs/architecture/decisions.md.
HOW IT IS MAINTAINED. Any change to the labre_mcp schema = one migration in labre
AND one update to this file, in the same batch. The field belongs functionally to
labre-mcp: the labre side is a cross-review.
PROVENANCE. Extracted from the LIVE local Supabase stack on 2026-08-26 by the
very introspection query schema-contract.test.mts runs (pg_catalog +
information_schema, container supabase_db_labre). Not hand-written from the
migrations — from the state they actually produce.
SCOPE OF THE GRANTS COMPARED. Roles anon / authenticated / service_role only
(the `postgres` owner is noise), privileges SELECT / INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE only.
REFERENCES / TRIGGER / TRUNCATE are deliberately out: `anon` still carries those
three on strategy_bundles as a residue of the public-schema defaults it was
relocated from (migration 20260711130000). They grant no read and no write; making
them part of the contract would freeze a wart instead of describing an invariant.

tables.name: api_keys
usedBy: The daemon never selects this table: it holds no credential that could.
constraints: FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE

tables.name: strategy_bundles
usedBy: storage_prefix, updated_at under the CALLER's JWT; `enabled` is what the RLS
policy filters on, so the policy below is part of the read contract, not decor.
constraints: FOREIGN KEY (created_by) REFERENCES auth.users(id) ON DELETE SET NULL

functions.name: create_api_key
usedBy: labre UI only — listed so a change to it is not invisible here.

functions.name: revoke_api_key
usedBy: labre UI only — listed so a change to it is not invisible here.

functions.name: validate_api_key
usedBy: Content-Profile: labre_mcp, under the PUBLIC anon key. `anon` on this EXECUTE
line is the daemon's whole door: revoke it and every lab_ bearer 401s. labre's
CLAUDE.md and supabase/tests/grants_coherence.sql both name it as a deliberate,
reviewed exception — this contract is the third guard, on the consumer side.
It returns SETOF (user_id uuid): a zero-row answer means unknown/revoked/expired.

storage: The `strategy-bundles` Storage bucket (private) and its single policy on
storage.objects — `strategy_bundles objects read`, SELECT to authenticated where
bucket_id = 'strategy-bundles' — are also read by supabase-bundle-source.mts.
They live in the `storage` schema, which is Supabase-managed surface: the same
reason labre's own grants_coherence.sql audits storage.objects and nothing else
there. Left out of the mechanical comparison on purpose; named here so the
dependency is not forgotten. Promote it if a bucket rename ever bites.
postgrestExposure: `labre_mcp` must appear in the project's PostgREST "Exposed schemas" (dashboard
setting, Settings → API) or every request above 404s regardless of grants. It is
not a schema object, so no introspection can assert it; migration
20260711130000 flags it as still MANUAL on prod.
